name: AWS Madison County (Mississippi)
analyst_notes: Two campuses across ~1,700 acres. Capex is Madison County only: the original $10B (Jan 2024) plus the $11B expansion (Apr 2026). Amazon's total Mississippi commitment is $25B including other sites. No MW disclosed.

name: AWS Mexico (Central) Region — Querétaro
analyst_notes: $5B is a 15-year commitment across three Querétaro data centers, not a single-site capex; AWS projects ~$10B GDP contribution and ~7,000 jobs. Region live since Jan 14, 2025 with AI/ML services framing; MW never disclosed. Querétaro also hosts Google and Microsoft regions — Mexico's datacenter epicenter, with drought/water scrutiny.

name: AWS Richmond County (North Carolina)
analyst_notes: ~800 acres, ~20 planned buildings, adjacent to Duke Energy's Smith Energy Complex. Largest single capital project in North Carolina history; broke ground July 2026. No MW disclosed.

name: AWS Salem Township (Susquehanna)
analyst_notes: Former Talen Cumulus campus adjacent to the Susquehanna nuclear plant, bought for $650M in Mar 2024 with ~240 MW developed at acquisition; ramping toward up to 960 MW site power. The 2025 Talen PPA covers up to 1,920 MW across AWS Pennsylvania sites. No source states the currently energized level, so nothing is recorded as confirmed.

name: Abilene Clean Campus (Crusoe)
analyst_notes: Tenancy is unsettled: OpenAI declined the expansion and Microsoft is reported to be in talks. Recorded as unattributed capacity rather than assigned to a tenant that has not signed.

name: AirTrunk SYD3
analyst_notes: AirTrunk (Blackstone) lists SYD3 at 330 MW+; industry trackers cite a >400 MW master plan. Serves hyperscale cloud/AI customers; anchor tenants not officially disclosed. Full campus not energized.

name: Aligned Project Caprock (Hale County)
analyst_notes: Capex null: release says 'The site is expected to infuse $5B into the regional economy' — regional economic impact, not stated construction capex. First data center LBB-01 'anticipated service date of Q1 2027.' Closed-loop cooling avoiding Ogallala Aquifer draw. Same county as the covered Fluidstack/Anthropic Abernathy campus but a separate project. Aligned itself was acquired in a ~$40B deal by the MGX/BlackRock-GIP AI Infrastructure Partnership (Oct 2025).

name: Applied Digital Polaris Forge 1 (Ellendale)
analyst_notes: Capex null per rules: the headline '$11B' is contracted lease revenue ('brings Applied Digital's total anticipated contracted lease revenue to approximately $11B'), not construction capex. 400MW is critical IT load (leases ~15 years, first two signed May-June 2025). Applied Digital is also developing Polaris Forge 2 (Harwood, ND). First 50MW came online 2025; Building 1 Phase 1 ready-for-service achieved for CoreWeave.

name: Bell AI Fabric (Kamloops cluster, with Groq)
analyst_notes: 500MW six-site target is ambition, not committed capacity: first 7MW Groq-equipped Kamloops site live June 2025, 7MW Merritt site and 26MW Thompson Rivers University facility (2026) plus second 26MW Kamloops facility (2027) committed; two further ~400MW-combined sites only 'in advanced planning'. Bloomberg reported (2026-06-18) BCE teaming with Cohere on a Canada AI data center, and (2026-03-16) CoreWeave/BCE backing a large western-Canada facility — expansion of this fabric.

name: ByteDance Johor (Sedenak Tech Park)
analyst_notes: Capex is the June 2024 RM10B (~$2.13B) AI-hub commitment; Johor officials put cumulative ByteDance datacenter investment above RM29.5B (~$6.6B) by Jan 2026, spread across own-build and leased capacity. Existing Sedenak facility operating, expansion ongoing. No site MW disclosed.

name: ByteDance Pecém AI datacenter campus (Omnia / Casa dos Ventos)
city: Caucaia / São Gonçalo do Amarante (Pecém port complex)
analyst_notes: ByteDance's largest datacenter outside China; R$200B (~US$38.4B) lifetime figure is the full multi-phase ambition — initial build is ~200MW IT (20 halls), with reported scaling to ~900MW-1GW by 2029. First reported by Reuters late 2025; construction began Jan 2026 (only pillars erected as of July 2026). Omnia (Pátria) signed a US$2B, 20-year wind PPA with Casa dos Ventos (630MW Ibiapaba complex). Local grid-strain scrutiny in Ceará. Capex omitted on review: the R$200B (~US$38.4B) figure is the full multi-phase lifetime ambition, not committed phase-one spend.

name: Campus IA (Fouju, Île-de-France)
analyst_notes: UAE-backed JV of MGX, Bpifrance, Mistral AI and NVIDIA, announced at Choose France 2025; site fixed at ZAC des Bordes, Fouju. Public inquiry under way per the prefecture (hence PERMITTING); construction planned from H2 2026, operations by 2028. Reported ~€8.5B initial investment not captured from a primary source, so no capex recorded.

name: Cassava AI Factory (Cape Town)
analyst_notes: Africa's first NVIDIA-powered 'AI factory', live March 2026 inside existing Africa Data Centres facilities — GPU-as-a-service, not a new-build campus, so no MW is recorded. The 12,000-GPU figure is a continent-wide acquisition claim, initial SA deployment reported around 3,000; neither is confirmed, so no GPU count is recorded. Johannesburg expansion planned.

name: China Telecom Lingang intelligent computing center
analyst_notes: 40,000 high-power racks planned in Lingang free-trade zone, mainly serving home-grown GPU development for Shanghai/Yangtze Delta AI firms. Per-site rack figure, no MW disclosed. Context: China Telecom is China's largest AIDC operator (900+ DCs, ~8GW total per company statements — aggregate, not this site).

name: China Telecom Shaoguan AI data center (Alibaba Zhenwu 10,000-chip cluster)
analyst_notes: Shaoguan is a Greater Bay Area national hub node under East Data West Computing. China Telecom owns/operates the facility; Alibaba supplies Zhenwu 810E accelerators (96GB HBM2e, T-Head architecture). Companies say the cluster is expected to expand to 100,000 chips; that expansion figure is a plan, not installed capacity.

name: Cipher Black Pearl (for AWS)
analyst_notes: Capex null: '~$5.5Bn Estimated Contract Value' is 15-year lease revenue, not construction capex. 300MW is gross power (site energized as front-of-the-meter bitcoin campus; Phase I 150MW mined BTC from Q2 2025). AWS also later revealed as tenant at Cipher's Stingray site ('a 70 MW critical IT load'). Cipher's separate Barber Lake site (244MW gross/168MW IT) is leased to Fluidstack with a $1.4B Google backstop, and its 1GW Colchis site is expected to energize in 2028.

name: CloudHQ Paulínia (GRU) Campus
analyst_notes: CloudHQ's first Latin America campus; press reports cite '$3.2B' but the sourced quote says 'more than $3 billion' — capex recorded at $3B floor. 225MW substation (expandable toward 400MW) energized; hyperscale AI/cloud tenants targeted. Roughly 100km from São Paulo metro.

name: CloudHQ QRO Campus Querétaro
analyst_notes: CloudHQ's largest single investment: six AI-oriented buildings (~US$800M each) on ~52ha, 900MW private substation + 2GW maneuvering substation, water-free cooling, LEED targets. Infrastructure delivery/first operations targeted 2027; ~7,000 construction jobs. Would be Mexico's largest hyperscale hub.

name: Compass Meridian
analyst_notes: 'The campus will consist of eight data centers that will be constructed over an eight-year period.' Compass leases build-to-suit to investment-grade hyperscalers; end tenant not officially disclosed (Meta widely speculated in trade press, unconfirmed). 500MW figure is utility supply (site power), not critical IT load. 10-year state tax exemptions granted.

name: Core Scientific Denton (CoreWeave)
analyst_notes: CoreWeave's largest contracted Core Scientific site (~260 MW critical IT load; 590 MW across six sites in the relationship, full delivery targeted early 2027). Converted bitcoin-mining site. The $1.2B figure is contracted hosting revenue, not capex, so no capex is recorded.

name: CoreWeave Cambridge (Cohere anchor)
analyst_notes: First investment under Canada's C$2B Sovereign AI Compute Strategy: up to C$240M federal financing toward Cohere's C$725M compute plan (figures in CAD, hence capexUsd null). CoreWeave operates the Cambridge facility, opened mid-2025; MW capacity undisclosed. Cohere has since also sourced Canadian compute via Bell's sovereign AI alliance (The Logic/Bloomberg, June 2026).

name: CoreWeave Lancaster
analyst_notes: Initial 100 MW expandable to 300 MW. Capex is CoreWeave's stated 'up to $6 billion' commitment.

name: Crusoe Goodnight (Armstrong County)
analyst_notes: Part of Google's November 2025 plan to 'invest $40 billion in Texas data centers' (Armstrong and Haskell counties) — capex null because $40B spans multiple sites. 'In January 2026, Crusoe filed a permit to build a 933 MW natural gas power plant onsite'; satellite imagery confirms two buildings under construction; first phase shares interconnection with a wind farm, segment due online in 2026. Third-party trackers list full build at ~1,030MW / 7 buildings / 3.4M sq ft. Distinct from Crusoe's covered Abilene (Stargate) campus and from Crusoe-Lancium's separately announced 1GW Childress partnership.

name: CyrusOne Freestone
analyst_notes: CyrusOne's largest single announced US AI campus; brings Constellation/Calpine-contracted CyrusOne capacity in Texas to 'a total of over 1100 MW under contract' including the earlier 400MW Whitney/Bosque County campus (DFW10, first building topped out March 2026) at Calpine's Thad Hill Energy Center. No online date disclosed.

name: DataVolt Oxagon AI Factory (NEOM)
analyst_notes: 1.5 GW total campus target, basis unstated; capex of $5B covers phase one only, with the first ~300 MW targeted for 2028. NEOM megaprojects have a documented history of rescoping and no construction on this campus is documented as of mid-2026 — treat scale as aspirational.

name: Deutsche Telekom Industrial AI Cloud (Munich)
analyst_notes: Opened February 2026 in a renovated Munich Tucherpark datacenter; ~€1B privately financed with NVIDIA. GPU count is DT's stated 'up to 10,000' ceiling (1,000+ DGX B200 systems). Facility MW not disclosed. Anchor customers reported include Mercedes-Benz, Siemens and BMW.

name: EcoCloud–G42 Olkaria Geothermal Campus
analyst_notes: Geothermal-powered campus with Microsoft as cloud partner (~$1B initial investment announced May 2024). Recorded at the 100 MW initial phase, not the 1 GW ceiling. Per May 2026 reporting the plan has stalled — the commissioning date was abandoned and government approval never materialized — hence PAUSED. A smaller ~60 MW KenGen-led project continues separately.

name: Edged–Merlin Extremadura Campuses
analyst_notes: Two campuses (Navalmoral de la Mata and Valdecaballeros) of up to 1 GW IT each, recorded as one combined 2 GW row matching the partners' joint announcement. Public–private with the regional government; no construction, tenant, capex or timeline confirmed — aspirational scale.

name: Fir Hills / Stock Farm Road 3GW AI data center, Jeollanam-do
owner: Fir Hills Inc (Stock Farm Road) with Jeollanam-do provincial government
city: Jeollanam-do (site not finalized in cited reports)
analyst_notes: Claimed 3GW / ~$35bn (KRW 50tn) campus by Brian Koo's Stock Farm Road vehicle Fir Hills, in partnership with Jeollanam-do provincial government; construction targeted from winter 2025, completion 2028. DCD framing ('claims') reflects skepticism; as of 2026 the project remains in pre-construction/structuring. Sometimes reported alongside a Jeonju (North Jeolla) proposal — cited sources place this project in Jeollanam-do. 3GW is planned capacity, basis not broken out. Status RUMORED on review: DCD frames the project as a claim and no construction is documented.

name: Firmus–DayOne Batam AI Factory
analyst_notes: Co-developed with DayOne; NVIDIA compute partnership through 2034, GPU deliveries through 2027–28. The cited $25–30B is committed offtake revenue, not capex. First operations targeted Q1 2027. GPU count is the announced deployment ceiling ('up to 170,000').

name: Fluidstack Abernathy
analyst_notes: Originally a TeraWulf–Fluidstack 51/49 JV (Google-backed); in July 2026 TeraWulf sold its stake to a Fluidstack-led group. 168 MW critical IT / 240 MW gross site power. Delivery expected H2 2026. Widely reported as the Texas site of Anthropic's $50B Fluidstack program.

name: Foxconn Kaohsiung AI Factory
analyst_notes: National AI factory with NVIDIA, TSMC and Taiwan's NSTC; phased 20→60→100 MW due to grid constraints, full deployment targeted 2026. Phase-1 energization not independently confirmed.

name: Galaxy Helios (Dickens County)
analyst_notes: Former bitcoin mine on 2,200+ acres; gross vs IT explicitly distinguished by Galaxy ('approximately 200 megawatts of gross power — 133 MW of critical IT load'). 15-year CoreWeave lease 'expected to generate more than $1 billion in average annual revenue' — lease revenue, not capex, hence capexUsd null. Phase I rent commenced Q2 2026. First CoreWeave lease announced March 2025 (month precision).

name: Google AI Hub Visakhapatnam
analyst_notes: Google's largest AI hub outside the US; $15B over 2026–2030 includes subsea cable gateway and clean energy. Foundation laid April 2026. 1 GW is 'compute capacity' with basis unstated. Partners AdaniConneX and Nxtra.

name: Google Cedar Rapids
analyst_notes: Google's second Iowa campus at Alliant Energy's Big Cedar Industrial Center; first building projected complete 2026, four more in later phases. $7B is statewide over two years, so no campus-level capex is recorded. No MW disclosed.

name: Google Cerrillos (Santiago)
analyst_notes: Cautionary status entry: 2020-permitted ~US$200M (reported) project abandoned in original form after Chile's Second Environmental Court partially revoked its permit over aquifer/water use (Feb 2024); Google committed to restart permitting 'from scratch' with air cooling and 24/7 carbon-free energy. No new approval as of mid-2026. Google's operational Chilean site remains Quilicura.

name: Google Stillwater
analyst_notes: New AI-focused campus on ~400 acres, phase one targeted 2027. The $9B figure is statewide (also expands the existing Pryor campus), so no campus-level capex is recorded. No MW disclosed.

name: Google West Memphis
analyst_notes: ~1,000-acre site powered by Entergy Arkansas; construction began Oct 2025 on an 18–24 month build. $4B through 2027 is the company-stated figure; local bond filings suggest the ultimate buildout could be far larger. No MW disclosed.

name: HUMAIN AI Factories Phase 1 (Riyadh & Dammam)
analyst_notes: PIF-backed sovereign program. 200 MW covers the two under-construction launch sites (up to 100 MW each, Riyadh and Dammam), basis unstated. The 500 MW NVIDIA target, a separate 500 MW AMD collaboration and the up-to-6 GW-by-2034 ambition are aspirational and not recorded as capacity. No source confirms energization as of late July 2026.

name: HUMAIN–xAI Data Center (Saudi Arabia)
analyst_notes: Announced at the US–Saudi investment forum; described as xAI's largest datacenter outside the US, for Grok training. Exact site, timeline and phasing undisclosed, so no coordinates are recorded. No construction documented as of July 2026.

name: Hut 8 River Bend (for Fluidstack)
analyst_notes: $7.0B is lease contract value (revenue, not capex); the $10B figure is LED's stated Phase I project investment. 'Google, a subsidiary of Alphabet Inc., is providing a financial backstop'; Fluidstack holds 'a Right of First Offer (ROFO) for up to an additional 1,000 MW of IT capacity.' Entergy providing '330 MW of utility capacity for the campus.' Initial data hall 'scheduled for completion and commissioning in Q2 2027.' Financed partly via $3.25B bond sale. Hut 8's GPU vertical operates as Highrise AI.

name: IREN Childress (Horizon, for Microsoft)
analyst_notes: '750 MW campus located in Childress, Texas.' $9.7B is contract value (cloud services revenue), not capex — capexUsd null; hardware funded partly via '$5.8 billion' Dell purchase agreement and a 20% Microsoft prepayment. Site began as grid-connected bitcoin campus (345kV). Horizon 1 (first GB300 cluster) handover targeted Q3 2026.

name: IREN Sweetwater
analyst_notes: Energization is the high-voltage substation connection to ERCOT, not operating IT capacity: 'Power delivery at Sweetwater 1 is expected to ramp progressively in line with the phased construction and commissioning of data centers.' Sweetwater 2 (600MW, ~28 miles away) targeted late 2027; the two sites are to be fiber-linked into a single 2GW hub. Coordinates approximate (town of Sweetwater).

name: Isambard-AI (Bristol)
analyst_notes: UK's most powerful supercomputer, fully launched July 2025, serving the UK AI Research Resource; 5,448 GH200 superchips. The 5 MW figure describes the operating facility, stated by the operator, hence recorded as confirmed. Capex converts the quoted £225M.

name: JUPITER (Jülich)
analyst_notes: Europe's first exascale system, inaugurated September 2025 and in operation; funded 50% EuroHPC JU, 50% German federal/NRW. Capex includes six years of operations. A ~18 MW power figure circulates from TOP500 data but no quotable source was captured, so no MW is recorded.

name: KDDI Osaka Sakai Data Center (former Sharp Sakai plant)
analyst_notes: Opened 2026-01-22 on part of Sharp's former Sakai LCD plant (KDDI bought its parcel for ~JPY10bn/US$68m in April 2025; GB200 NVL72 racks, direct liquid cooling, 100% renewable power). Distinct from SoftBank's separate 150MW project on the larger portion of the same Sharp Sakai site (already covered). 48MW is facility capacity as reported at launch; IT-vs-total basis not broken out.

name: Lambda Kansas City
analyst_notes: Retrofit of a vacant facility; $500M per Missouri economic-development reporting. 24 MW at launch, potential to scale past 100 MW; energization not publicly confirmed as of July 2026. Announcement date approximate (Nov 2025).

name: Meta El Paso
analyst_notes: Broke ground Oct 2025. On 2026-07-28 Meta and BlackRock (with GIP and HPS) announced a JV owning the campus — BlackRock funds 80%, Meta 20%, ~$14B total development cost. Capacity online from 2028. Reported to rely partly on on-site natural gas generation.

name: Meta Hyperion
analyst_notes: 5 GW is a full-build target across many phases, not near-term capacity. Treated as an estimate; no phase is confirmed energised in the sources reviewed.

name: Meta Lebanon (Indiana)
analyst_notes: Groundbreaking 2026-02-11; Meta's 27th US data center. Reported full operation late 2027/early 2028, recorded as no date since sources give a range. 1 GW basis (IT vs site) not specified.

name: Meta Prometheus
analyst_notes: Nuclear agreements with TerraPower, Oklo and Vistra are power-purchase commitments, not on-site reactors delivering today.

name: Microsoft Fairwater — Atlanta
analyst_notes: Paired with the Wisconsin site; the two are reported to operate as a single distributed training fabric.

name: Microsoft Fairwater — Wisconsin
analyst_notes: Closed-loop liquid cooling, reported to eliminate operational water consumption. Reported as exceeding 350 MW and scaling further, so 350 MW is a floor rather than a point estimate.

name: Microsoft India South Central (Hyderabad)
analyst_notes: Flagship of Microsoft's $17.5B 2026–2029 India commitment (country-wide figure, so no site capex recorded). Three availability zones; targeted live mid-2026. No site MW disclosed.

name: Microsoft Pecos
analyst_notes: Reeves County, West Texas. ~2 GW served by a co-located behind-the-meter natural gas facility; 'multibillion-dollar' investment over five to seven years, no specific capex stated. Basis (IT vs site) not stated. Distinct from the Fairwater sites.

name: Microsoft–Khazna UAE Expansion
analyst_notes: Part of Microsoft's $15.2B UAE commitment through 2029 (country-wide figure, so no capex recorded here). Khazna groundbreakings in Abu Dhabi support under-construction status; specific sites for the full 200 MW not disclosed. Distinct from Stargate UAE.

name: NAVER GAK Sejong AI Factory
analyst_notes: NAVER states a long-term ambition to reach 1 GW of NVIDIA AI infrastructure. That is an intent, not a committed build, and is deliberately NOT counted in the capacity figures — only the announced 200 MW by 2028 is. Funding split: Brookfield up to $9B as exclusive capital partner, NVIDIA $1B, NAVER the remainder.

name: Nebius Béthune
analyst_notes: Redevelopment of a former Bridgestone tyre plant near Lille. Reuters: first capacity online by late summer 2026 and roughly half the site operational by end of 2026. Nebius did not disclose cost; third-party estimates are excluded.

name: Nebius Highridge (Pennsylvania)
analyst_notes: Nebius's second US gigawatt-scale campus, Schuylkill County; ~3-year build, still in local approvals as of July 2026. 1.2 GW is grid supply from PPL (site power, not stated as IT load).

name: Nebius Lappeenranta AI Factory
analyst_notes: Nebius's largest facility outside the US, on a ~100-acre industrial site. Press reports value the project above $10B but that is not in the primary release, so no capex is recorded. Distinct from Nebius's operational Mäntsälä site.

name: Nebius Vineland
analyst_notes: Phased development to 300 MW design capacity (basis not stated as IT load). Anchor for Nebius's ~$17.4B Microsoft dedicated-capacity agreement; first phases energized, full 300 MW not confirmed operating.

name: Nexus AI Factory Morocco
analyst_notes: Consortium with NAVER, NVIDIA and Lloyd Capital; first phase 40 MW with GB200s, staged toward a 500 MW target; renewable supply via TAQA. Construction start not independently confirmed, so ANNOUNCED. Would be among Africa's largest AI facilities.

name: Nscale Barstow (Texas, for Microsoft)
analyst_notes: Site leased from Ionic Digital; fourth Nscale–Microsoft deal, reported at up to $24B (contract value, not capex). Construction from Q3 2026; Microsoft holds an option for a further 700 MW from Q1 2027. 240 MW initial, expandable to 1.2 GW; basis unstated. GPU count is the announced deployment plan.

name: Nscale Loughton (for Microsoft)
analyst_notes: Billed as the UK's largest AI supercomputer when live, serving Microsoft Azure. 90 MW is the scalable ceiling (50 MW initial). GPU count is the announced initial deployment for Q1 2027. Part of Nscale's ~200,000-GB300 Microsoft contract across Europe and the US.

name: Ooredoo Sovereign AI Cloud (Doha)
analyst_notes: First NVIDIA Cloud Partner sovereign AI cloud in Qatar, live since ~July 2025 in existing Ooredoo/Syntys facilities. Dedicated MW and GPU count undisclosed, so no figures are recorded. Syntys's >120 MW / ~$1B plan is a group datacenter target, not this deployment.

name: OpenAI–Tata HyperVault (India)
analyst_notes: OpenAI is the first customer of TCS's HyperVault data-center business: 100 MW initially, with plans to scale to 1 GW. Site undisclosed, so no coordinates are recorded. Part of Stargate per OpenAI.

name: Poolside Project Horizon (Fort Stockton)
analyst_notes: 2GW campus on 568 acres of the Mitchell family's Longfellow Ranch, gas-rich Permian Basin site. CoreWeave was anchor tenant (15-yr lease, 250MW first phase expandable to 500MW, planned 40,000+ GB300 NVL72 GPUs) but the deal was mutually terminated in early 2026; Poolside approached other clouds incl. Google ('Google is no longer in talks with Poolside'). Power figure is planned gross site power, none operating.

name: Project Rainier
analyst_notes: Reported at roughly 1 GW or more of IT power. IT load and site power are different quantities and the sources are not always explicit about which is meant.

name: Prometheus Hyperscale Evanston
analyst_notes: 506-acre site on founder Trenton Thornock's family ranch; unanimous Uinta County conditional-use approval June 2026. 'Prometheus says construction will begin within six months of final permitting and take four to five years.' Mostly natural-gas powered, closed-loop water-glycol cooling. Capex null: reported $30B covers two Wyoming projects (Evanston plus a proposed Casper-area site), not this campus alone. Former BP CEO Bernard Looney leads the buildout. Some reports cite expansion potential to 5GW.

name: QTS–Lancium Hall County
analyst_notes: Up to 11 QTS-built buildings on 465 acres at Lancium's Clean Campus; 'The site is supported by a 1GW grid connection.' On-site solar plus battery storage, closed-loop cooling; up to 7,000 peak construction jobs, ~350 permanent. No construction start or opening dates announced. Separate from Blackstone/QTS's $25B Pennsylvania commitment and the abandoned 2,100-acre Virginia Digital Gateway.

name: Reliance Jamnagar AI Campus
analyst_notes: Media reports of up to 3 GW / 'world's largest' ambitions are unconfirmed by Reliance filings, so the 1 GW planned figure is used, basis unstated. A Meta–Reliance JV anchors a reported 168 MW lease at Jamnagar. A separate MOU for a twin 1 GW campus in Andhra Pradesh is MOU-stage and not recorded.

name: SK Telecom–AWS Ulsan AI Data Center
analyst_notes: Groundbreaking Aug 2025; AWS anchor tenant. First phase 41 MW by Nov 2027, expanding to 103 MW by Feb 2029; basis unstated. The $5.88B figure is AWS's Korea-wide investment, so no site capex is recorded. SKT's July 2026 15 GW-by-2035 regional plan is aspirational and not recorded.

name: Sakura Internet Ishikari GPU data center expansion
analyst_notes: ~2,000 H100s operational at Ishikari (NVIDIA PR: expanding 'from 2,000 to nearly 4,000 NVIDIA Hopper GPUs'); HGX B200 planned toward ~10,800 total GPUs. Company added ~1,100 Blackwell GPUs in a container DC at Ishikari announced 2026-02-24 (company announcement). Backed by ~JPY50.1bn METI subsidy for national GenAI compute; site targeted fully renewable by 2027. gpuCount reflects confirmed installed H100 base, not targets.

name: Scala AI City (Phase 1)
analyst_notes: Aspirational full build is 4.75GW ('4.750MW distribuídos em mais de 7 milhões de metros quadrados') — among the largest DC ambitions in the Americas; MME granted a 5GW grid-reserve authorization, one of Brazil's largest ever. Only the 54MW/US$500M Phase 1 is committed; construction started after Eldorado do Sul enabling law was sanctioned. 100% renewable, PUE <=1.2 claimed, Malbec subsea-cable connectivity.

name: SoftBank France AI Program (Hauts-de-France)
analyst_notes: Announced at Choose France 2026. Program across three sites (Loon-Plage/Dunkirk, Bosquel, Bouchain); capex is the USD equivalent of the up-to-€75B pledge, phase one €45B for 3.1 GW by 2031. Program-stage — no construction confirmed. Coordinates are the Loon-Plage lead site.

name: SoftBank Sakai AI Data Center
analyst_notes: Conversion of Sharp's former Sakai LCD plant; over 150 MW initially with a stated path to over 400 MW. Capex is the property purchase (~$676M), not full fit-out. Original 2025 target slipped to 2026. Linked to the SB OpenAI Japan JV (Cristal Intelligence workloads).

name: Stargate Abilene
analyst_notes: Gas turbines rated up to ~300 MW are reported on site, bridging the gap while grid capacity is built.

name: Stargate Argentina (Patagonia)
analyst_notes: Letter-of-intent stage: OpenAI and Sur Energy signed an LOI, up to $25B under Argentina's RIGI incentive regime. 'Up to 500 MW'; exact location and start date undisclosed, so no coordinates are recorded.

name: Stargate Doña Ana County
analyst_notes: Site confirmed by OpenAI's own announcement; no per-site capacity was published, so power is deliberately left blank rather than guessed.

name: Stargate Korea — SK (Jeollanam-do)
analyst_notes: MOU stage only; exact site still being selected at announcement, so no coordinates are recorded. Shares the reported 20 MW combined initial capacity with the Samsung/Pohang site, so no per-site power claim is recorded.

name: Stargate Korea — Samsung (Pohang)
analyst_notes: MOU/LOI stage only, signed 2025-10-01 during Altman's Seoul visit; no binding construction contract published. The reported 20 MW initial capacity is combined across both Korean sites, so no per-site power claim is recorded.

name: Stargate Lordstown
analyst_notes: Site confirmed by OpenAI; no per-site capacity published.

name: Stargate Michigan (Saline Township)
analyst_notes: Developed by Related Digital for OpenAI/Oracle; DTE Energy supply plan approved at 1.4 GW (site power). The companies' own announcement says 'more than a gigawatt' of capacity. Groundbreaking held 2026-06-01. Capex ~$16B per press reports, not confirmed by the companies.

name: Stargate Milam County
analyst_notes: Site confirmed by OpenAI; no per-site capacity published.

name: Stargate Norway (Kvandal, Narvik)
analyst_notes: Nscale-Aker 50/50 JV, OpenAI offtaker; first European OpenAI-for-Countries site. Hydropower-fed. Capacity basis (IT vs site) not specified. The 100,000-GPU figure is a target, not a deployed count, recorded as an estimate, matching how other announced site targets are held. Both parties committed ~$1B to the initial 20 MW phase only.

name: Stargate Shackelford County
analyst_notes: 1.4 GW is stated as IT capacity, which is not the same as site power draw. Recorded as IT capacity and flagged, because the two are routinely conflated in reporting.

name: Stargate UAE
suppliers: OpenAI (OPERATOR); Oracle (OPERATOR); NVIDIA (GPU_SUPPLIER); Cisco (NETWORKING_SUPPLIER); SoftBank Group (INVESTOR)
analyst_notes: The 1 GW cluster sits inside a wider 5 GW UAE–US AI Campus. Only the 1 GW cluster is counted here — counting the campus envelope as well would double-count the same megawatts.

name: Stargate UK (Cobalt Park, North Tyneside)
analyst_notes: Announced Sept 2025; PAUSED April 2026 over UK energy costs and AI copyright rules, with no construction started. The 8,000/31,000 GPU figures were offtake exploration targets, never deployed, so no GPU claim is recorded. No MW figure was ever disclosed.

name: Stargate Wisconsin (Vantage Lighthouse)
analyst_notes: One of the five Stargate sites announced 2025-09-23. 902 MW across four buildings per local reporting of the approved plan; Vantage's own words are 'close to a gigawatt of AI capacity' (IT). Site draw reported at 1.3 GW with later phases potentially to 3.5 GW. Groundbreaking Dec 2025, completion scheduled 2028.

name: TELUS Sovereign AI Factory (Rimouski)
analyst_notes: Rimouski, QC facility operational Sept 2025 (NVIDIA Cloud Partner, HPE-built). May 2026: B.C. cluster announced — Kamloops expansion plus two Vancouver Westbank sites (M3 Mount Pleasant end-2026; 150 West Georgia 2029), >150MW/>60,000 GPUs by 2032 is a plan, not built. Quebec context: Hydro-Québec has restricted new >5MW data-centre allocations and proposed roughly doubling their rate (~13c/kWh) effective H2 2026 — a headwind for new Quebec builds. Power and GPU figures omitted on review: the Rimouski facility MW is undisclosed, and the >150 MW / 60,000-GPU figures are the 2032 British Columbia expansion plan, not built capacity.

name: TeraWulf Justified (Anthropic lease)
analyst_notes: Anthropic is the direct tenant on a 20-year lease (~$19B contracted revenue — revenue, not capex). Initial capacity H2 2027, full 401 MW critical IT load by early 2028. Part of Anthropic's US compute buildout alongside the Fluidstack program.

name: TeraWulf Lake Mariner (Fluidstack/Anthropic)
analyst_notes: Former bitcoin mine on Lake Ontario converted to AI. Fluidstack leases total ~360 MW critical IT load; Google backstops ~$3.2B of Fluidstack obligations. Widely reported as the New York site of Anthropic's $50B Fluidstack program, though Anthropic's announcement does not name Lake Mariner.

name: Tesla Cortex (Giga Texas)
analyst_notes: Cortex 1 operational since 2024 at ~130 MW launch draw with 50,000 H100s shown; 500 MW is the stated full site-power target for the Cortex 2.0 expansion (reported mid-2026 completion). Larger 2026 GPU-count claims circulate only in weak sources and are not recorded.

name: Ubilink.AI supercomputing center (Foxlink/Ubitus/Shinfox, NVIDIA cloud partner)
owner: Ubilink (JV of Foxlink, Ubitus, Shinfox Energy)
city: Taipei (exact district not disclosed in cited sources)
analyst_notes: Billed as Taiwan's largest commercial AI supercomputing facility at launch (Nov 2024): 128 ASUS-built NVIDIA HGX H100 servers / 1,024 GPUs, 45.82 PFLOPS (TOP500 #31, Green500 #44), PUE 1.2, renewable-energy options via Shinfox. Partners state expansion toward ~10,240 H100/B100/B200 GPUs — plan, not installed. Distinct from the already-covered Foxconn/NVIDIA Kaohsiung AI factory. Caveat: coverage is company-announcement and Taiwanese trade press; limited Western trade-press verification, flagged per provenance rules.

name: Volcano Cloud Taihang Computing Centre Phase II (ByteDance)
analyst_notes: 4.5bn yuan (US$614m) campus in Guangling County Economic Development Zone Big Data Park, eastern Datong; 205,013 sqm, six two-storey DC buildings plus one six-storey integrated facility. SCMP reports 15,604 12kW server cabinets plus 510 network cabinets (implies ~187MW IT load, not stated as such — powerMw left null). Supports Doubao AI workloads; Datong ranked third nationally on CAICT computing-power index.

name: Wonder Valley AI Data Centre Industrial Park (Phase 1)
city: Greenview Industrial Gateway (south of Grande Prairie)
analyst_notes: Aspirational: developer pitches 7.5GW over 5-10 years and 'over $70 billion' lifetime investment, but as of Dec 2025 land purchase was not finalized, no new provincial permits filed, and construction is not expected before late 2028 (The Logic). 2026 earmarked for environmental/AUC permitting. Only Phase 1 (1.4GW, ~US$2B) recorded here; treat all capacity as unbuilt ambition. Recorded at the Phase 1 figure only; treat as unbuilt ambition per The Logic reporting.

name: YTL Green Data Center Park
analyst_notes: 1,640-acre campus ~30 km from Singapore; 500 MW planned park capacity paired with a co-located 500 MW solar plant. Malaysia's first NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 AI datacenter (YTL AI Cloud) operational since Oct 2025; full park capacity not energized.

name: Yiwu County government-backed AI data center complex
gpu_model: NVIDIA H100/H200 (planned per filings; sourcing unclear under export controls)
analyst_notes: AGGREGATE CAVEAT: the >115,000 Nvidia H100/H200 figure covers 39 data center projects approved in Q4 2024 across Xinjiang and Qinghai, per Bloomberg's review of filings — not one site. Bloomberg reports roughly 70% of planned compute is concentrated in this single government-backed complex near Yiwu (implying ~80k chips), powered by wind, solar and coal with free-electricity incentives. Chip sourcing path unverified; construction/tenders underway on 7 of 39 projects as of mid-2025.

name: Z.ai (Zhipu) 1GW AI computing centre
gpu_model: Chinese domestic accelerators (vendor not named; Huawei Ascend implied)
analyst_notes: Facility in partial operation as of July 2026; 1GW figure is company-stated design capacity, IT-vs-site basis not specified. Site location not disclosed in Bloomberg/SCMP reporting — coordinates are Z.ai's Beijing HQ, not the DC. Z.ai has been on the US entity list since Jan 2025; also runs multiple 10,000+ chip clusters. GLM-5.2 reportedly trained entirely on Huawei Ascend. Coordinates omitted: the site location is undisclosed.

name: eStruxture CAL-3
analyst_notes: Tier III design, up to 125kW/rack densities. CoreWeave signed as Phase 1 anchor tenant May 14, 2026 — its second Canadian site. eStruxture frames CAL-3 as part of 'more than C$1 billion' Alberta investment; capex here is the CA$750M (US$540M) CAL-3 figure.

name: xAI Colossus 1
analyst_notes: Original Colossus at the former Electrolux plant, operational since 2024. 300 MW is facility power consumption for the completed Phase 2 buildout, not on-site generation (the site separately has ~150 MW of Megapack buffering and gas turbines). 2026 reporting says Colossus 1 now serves inference while training moved to Colossus 2.

name: xAI Colossus 2
analyst_notes: On-site generation is the defining feature: the site sidesteps the interconnection queue, which is why its timeline is faster than grid-dependent peers.

name: xAI MACROHARDRR (Southaven)
analyst_notes: Third Colossus-complex building, announced by Musk on X 2025-12-30; warehouse conversion under way through 2026. The ~2 GW figure is the stated target for the whole Memphis-area complex, not this building, so no power is recorded here.
